cases.title: A copper–silver cell links two different electron stoichiometries
cases.original_expected_result: The silver electrode is the more positive reduction half-cell; copper oxidation coupled to silver reduction has a positive forward driving force.

original_expected_processes.interpretation: Educational chemical equation, not an assertion that the runtime implements every species or pathway.

cases.script:
# RX-011: A copper–silver cell links two different electron stoichiometries
# Candidate experiment; expected observations are not measured results.
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 CuSO4 0.001mol
add v1 Cu 1g
new
add v2 water 100mL
add v2 AgNO3 0.001mol
add v2 Ag 1g
cell v1 v2
inspect

criteria.observations: Runtime identifies v1 Cu as anode and v2 Ag as positive cathode; voltage 0.4080887599150608 V. Positive value is cathode minus anode, not a signed input-lead convention.

original.criterion: Identify which electrode is positive using the runtime sign convention rather than guessing the order of printed signs.

criteria.observations: Every cell call leaves all published vessel state unchanged relative to its preceding snapshot. No discharge or metal consumption is assigned to voltage measurement.

original.criterion: Only open-circuit potential is expected; no two-silver-per-copper discharge is performed by cell.

ledger.scope: Final whole-script and per-vessel represented material/charge, with explicit input amounts, trapped air and gas exports. Filter transfers only the previously owned liquid/aqueous portions. No solver species, free H/OH diagnostics, historical lots or solute_charge double counting; no energy/per-step closure claim.

qualifications: Ideal open-circuit Nernst calculation, ideal salt bridge and no junction potential; E0 is used at vessel temperature without dE0/dT. Zinc is below the hydrogen line and mixed-potential/passivation rates are outside this model. No empirical electrode calibration; full paired snapshots and named limits are retained.

cases.title: A zinc concentration cell reverses sign when electrodes are swapped
cases.original_expected_result: The concentration difference generates a non-zero voltage, and reversing the electrode order reverses its sign without changing the chemistry.
cases.script:
# RX-012: A zinc concentration cell reverses sign when electrodes are swapped
# Candidate experiment; expected observations are not measured results.
register lv3
add v1 water 100mL
add v1 ZnSO4 0.0001mol
add v1 Zn 1g
new
add v2 water 100mL
add v2 ZnSO4 0.01mol
add v2 Zn 1g
cell v1 v2
cell v2 v1
inspect

criteria.observations: Both reversed calls report +0.04003851213353726 V, anode v1 and cathode v2. Original opposite-sign expectation is not met. Source cell() explicitly sorts electrode potentials and reports a positive spontaneous EMF magnitude; not an established engine sign bug.

original.criterion: The two readings have approximately equal magnitudes and opposite signs.

criteria.observations: Nernst comparison uses reported Zn activities 0.0006922 and 0.01604 at actual temperatures 298.1692633 and 300.0761572 K, not nominal 100-fold ZnSO4 molarity. Activities have report rounding; no exact equality or new numerical pass band is asserted. Source uses resolved free-ion activity in electrode().

original.criterion: Use zinc activity, not just nominal ZnSO4 molarity, for a Nernst comparison.

ledger.scope: Final whole-script and per-vessel represented material/charge, with explicit input amounts, trapped air and gas exports. Filter transfers only the previously owned liquid/aqueous portions. No solver species, free H/OH diagnostics, historical lots or solute_charge double counting; no energy/per-step closure claim.

qualifications: Ideal open-circuit Nernst calculation, ideal salt bridge and no junction potential; E0 is used at vessel temperature without dE0/dT. Zinc is below the hydrogen line and mixed-potential/passivation rates are outside this model. No empirical electrode calibration; full paired snapshots and named limits are retained.
